If Δ = 0, there is one real root, x = -b / (2a). If Δ < 0, there are no real roots.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions to this equation are the x-values of the stationary points. To determine whether each stationary point is a maximum, minimum, or a saddle point, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x), and evaluate it at each stationary point. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the point is a saddle point.
